result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You had a breast X-ray (breast screening mammogram). The clinic needs you to come back for more tests. This is called a recall.

Being called back does not mean that you have cancer. About 4 in 5 women who are called back do not have breast cancer.

At the appointment, you may have more breast X-rays (mammograms). You may have an ultrasound scan. In some cases, you may have a biopsy. This means they take a small sample of tissue. Which tests you have may vary.

You will usually get most of your results on the same day. The visit may take up to 4 hours.

## What you need to do
1. Go to your appointment at the Breast Assessment Clinic, Eastmoor Hospital. The clinic has already booked it for you.
2. If you cannot come, call 01632 960 733 as soon as possible.
3. You can bring a friend or family member with you if you want to. You do not have to.

## Dates and medicines
- 16 September 2026: your breast X-ray (breast screening mammogram).
- Wednesday 7 October 2026 at 11:00: your appointment at the Breast Assessment Clinic, Eastmoor Hospital.
- The letter does not list any medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- Which tests will I have at the appointment?
- What is an ultrasound scan?
- When will I get any results that are not ready on the same day?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
